proof_summary: For an odd proper prime divisor \(p\mid n\), LTE applied at multiples of \(d=\operatorname{ord}_p(2)\) gives enough \(p\)-adic valuation to prove \(p\mid a(n-1)\), contradicting the assumed divisibility; composites with no odd prime divisor are powers \(2^s\), excluded by the exact valuation \(v_2(a(2^s-1))=s-1\). Once \(n=p\) is prime, Wilson’s theorem turns the congruence into \(\prod_{k=1}^{p-2}(2^k-1)=1\pmod p\); since \(\operatorname{ord}_p(2)\mid p-1\), any smaller order would make one factor zero, so the order is \(p-1\).
